previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her 17th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well with no significant side effects. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately, falling below 0.1 by discharge, with no renal toxicity. Liver enzymes showed mild, expected elevation. A recent brain MRI confirmed stable disease without new lesions. Due to her history of DVT and PE, aspirin was held during admission to optimize methotrexate excretion and was restarted at discharge. She remained emotionally stable on citalopram, with no depressive symptoms. Chronic right foot pain was managed with gabapentin and PRN oxycodone. She was discharged home in good condition with instructions to restart aspirin and follow up for her next chemotherapy cycle.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ woman with UC, asthma, DVT/PE, and CNS lymphoma admitted

*ACTIVE ISSUES*
# CNS lymphoma: Restaging MRI before the start of this cycle 
showed stable disease. Given ___ cycle #18 high-dose MTX 
8g/m2.  Alkalinization with sodium bicarbonate PO and IV fluids 
to enhance methotrexate excretion.  Leucovorin rescue to start 
24hrs after MTX given.  Followed MTX levels daily starting 24hrs 
after MTX given.  Home when MTX <0.20.  Anti-emetics pre-meds 
and PRN.  She tolerated this cycle very well. Mild transaminitis 
noted again this cycle. Monitor with next cycle. MTX level at 
discharge was 0.07, so did not need to take any extra leucovorin 
or sodium bicarbonate.  Dr. ___ plans to start Rituxan and 
will follow-up with patient in clinic.
.
# Right foot pain/right leg weakness: Chronic, unclear etiology. 
Continued outpatient gabapentin 800mg TID and PRN 
oxycodone/acetaminophen. Encouraged to follow up with PCP, who 
can manage the pain or refer as necessary.
.
*CHRONIC ISSUES*
# Ulcerative colitis: Stable throughout hospital course. GI 
consulted during her admission for cycle #17 given UC flare. She 
had a colonoscopy ___ at ___ which showed mild 
proctitis, remainder of colon normal. She was switched from PO 
mesalamine to PR dosing and hematochezia resolved quickly. She 
has been off these medications since that time. 
.
# Depression: Controlled.  Continued outpatient citalopram.
.
# LLE DVT/PE: Stopped enoxaparin ___ and changed to aspirin 
per Neuro-oncologist Dr. ___.  Held aspirin to enhance MTX 
excretion.  Restarted at discharge.  
.
# Anemia: Chemo-induced.  Mild, stable.
.
# Asthma: Chronic, controlled.  Continued outpatient 
fluticasone/salmeterol, montelukast, albuterol/ipratropium.
.
*TRANSITIONAL ISSUES*
- Right foot pain: unclear etiology, may not be chemo-related. 
Encouraged for workup with PCP and referral to specialist as 
necessary.

MP-RAGE, axial T1 FLAIR post, axial T1 post, axial FSE T2,and axial T2 trace.

the FLAIR images, there is stable hyperintensity surrounding the right frontal
lobe encephalomalacia.

There is no new lesion or abnormal enhancement.

There are scattered nonspecific foci of FLAIR hyperintensity in the
subcortical and periventricular white matter.  There is no acute infarct or
new hemorrhage.

There is no mass effect, or hydrocephalus.

There is persistent frontal, sphenoid, and ethmoidal inflammatory sinus
disease.  There is a retention cyst within the right maxillary sinus.

The intracranial flow voids are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  
No evidence of lymphoma recurrence. 

There is chronic paranasal inflammatory sinus disease.
